historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management guidance (FY2026 high-single-digit revenue/gross-bookings growth algorithm), cross-checked against the 3yr revenue CAGR (16.3%, inflated by the FY2022-23 post-COVID travel-demand snapback) and the less-distorted 6yr FY2019-FY2025 CAGR (10.2%, spans the COVID trough but is the closest available normal-cycle anchor). Equity CAGR is NOT used: shareholders' equity is deeply negative (~-$10.8B) from cumulative buybacks and is not a meaningful growth signal for this business, per the task routing and SKILL.md.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR (29.5%) diverges sharply from revenue 3yr CAGR (16.3%) -- driven almost entirely by the buyback-funded share count reduction (>40% since 2014) compounding on top of operating growth, not a margin or accounting anomaly. This is the expected signature of BKNG's capital-return model and is explicitly not charged twice in this DCF: buybacks are value-neutral in the owner-FCF framework (SBC is expensed once in the flows; the share count is held flat rather than being credited twice for both the SBC expense and the resulting buyback-driven EPS accretion).

scenario_narratives.base: Management's own high-single-digit growth algorithm holds; Transformation Program savings land on schedule by FY2027; Connected Trip and AI initiatives sustain modest, unspectacular margin expansion without needing any single bet to be transformative.
scenario_narratives.bull: Connected Trip, AI and alternative-accommodations initiatives compound faster than guided, Genius loyalty defends the traffic funnel against AI-search disintermediation, and the EU DMA transition proves a manageable compliance cost rather than a structural profit headwind.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI-search disintermediation structurally erodes the paid-search funnel BKNG depends on, EU DMA/antitrust litigation proves a genuine structural cost, and travel demand growth normalizes to low-single-digit -- margin compresses from 37.8% toward the mid-30s permanently, though the business stays solidly cash-generative throughout.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Booking Holdings is valued on a strict owner-FCF component-build DCF (10-year explicit horizon, since the year-1 owner-FCF margin of ~25.8% is still climbing toward its Transformation-Program-driven mature level of ~28% by year 9-10). Stockholders' equity is deeply negative (~-$10.8B) from over a decade of aggressive, sustained buybacks (>40% share-count reduction since 2014), which rules out any book-value-dependent model -- this DCF is built entirely from revenue, margin and net-debt anchors, with the flat post-split fully-diluted share count and net-debt bridge doing the work a book-value model would otherwise do. The single most consequential modelling choice in this build is NOT using the naive reported-FCF-derived owner FCF (~$7.94B, 29.5% margin) as the base year: roughly $1.7-2.2B of FY2025 operating cash flow is non-cash, non-operating noise -- principally a $1.4B unrealized FX loss on Euro-denominated debt that reversed to a $0.5B gain the prior year -- and the component build instead anchors to the company's own disclosed Adjusted-EBITDA-before-SBC margin (37.8%) to produce a cleaner $6.8B/25.4%-margin base year that will not swing $2B on currency noise. A 25-for-1 stock split effected 2026-04-02 is fully reflected: all share counts, the price and per-share outputs here are post-split.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI-driven search (Google AI Overviews, emerging AI travel agents) structurally disintermediating the paid-search funnel BKNG has monetized for two decades
EU Digital Markets Act gatekeeper obligations and 10,000+-hotel parity-clause litigation, with DMA fines of up to 10-20% of global annual revenue for non-compliance

The FX/convertible-note non-cash swing that motivated the component-build reconciliation is itself a real economic exposure (Euro-denominated debt) even though it is excluded from the unlevered owner-FCF base -- a sustained USD/EUR move affects reported net income and GAAP leverage optics even where it does not affect operating cash generation
Deeply negative stockholders' equity reduces balance-sheet flexibility in a sharp, sustained travel downturn despite low net debt/EBITDA today

Working-capital tailwind assumed at zero (not negative) -- if merchant-model mix shift accelerates faster than modelled, receivables growth could outpace deferred-merchant-bookings growth and turn working capital into a modest headwind

data_sources.financials: SEC EDGAR: FY2025 10-K (bkng-20251231.htm, filed 2026-02, CIK 0001075531) and Q2 2026 10-Q (bkng-20260630.htm, filed 2026-07-27) primary financial statements, MD&A and notes (Treasury Stock and Dividends, Segment Information, Stock Split); cross-checked against research/BKNG/Reports/BKNG_Metrics.csv and dcf_context.py's kpis pivot (equity_award_taxes, buybacks, cash_taxes series)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares, Q2 2026 10-Q (770M), post 25-for-1 stock split effected 2026-04-02; held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in owner FCF (charging both would double-count). Cover-page basic count at 2026-07-27 was 751.38M; the diluted weighted-average is the more conservative (higher) divisor and matches the dilutive-securities convention.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 income statement (Personnel line discloses SBC of $613M) + Treasury Stock and Dividends note (employee withholding taxes remitted $530M FY2025). Booking does not publish one combined 'SBC related to equity awards' reconciliation line, so the two are summed per method 1(a): $613M + $530M = $1,147M, 4.26% of FY2025 revenue.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:01Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 150.14-224.996 (post-split basis throughout, no discontinuity)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.0% base: large-cap, globally diversified (Europe/APAC-weighted), asset-light online travel marketplace with real but moderate cyclicality (discretionary travel demand) and modest leverage (net debt/EBITDA ~0.3x). Built on a USD risk-free rate + equity risk premium consistent with a mature US-listed consumer-internet compounder; below the 10-12% used for small/micro-cap or distressed names in this folder, above a true low-risk monopoly. Bull 8.5% (thesis de-risks if it plays out), bear 10.0% (AI-search disintermediation and EU DMA/antitrust overhang are real tail risks).
inputs.lease_treatment: Not material — BKNG's operating lease assets/liabilities are small (~$594M/$514M vs $29.7B total assets); no separate lease adjustment applied, consistent with an asset-light online marketplace.
inputs.nci_treatment: None — Booking Holdings has no reported non-controlling interests.
inputs.notes: OWNER-FCF DCF via the component route (Step 2 SKILL.md routing: mature, highly cash-generative internet/marketplace operating company). Stockholders' equity is deeply negative (~-$10.8B at Q2 2026) from a decade-plus of aggressive buybacks; per the task brief and the routing table this rules out any book-value-dependent model, so growth/margin/net-debt anchors are used throughout and equity CAGR is NOT used as a growth-rate input. STOCK SPLIT: Booking effected a 25-for-1 stock split on 2026-04-02, retroactively restated in the Q1/Q2 2026 10-Qs. All share counts, EPS and the current price in this file are POST-SPLIT. The BKNG_Metrics.csv SharesOutstanding column has a units artifact from this split: Q1 2025/Q2 2025 rows (827/815) are an SEC XBRL duplicate-context tag reporting a full-year annualized/adjusted count under the same period, NOT a real share count error; FY2025 and Q3 2025 rows (32.6/32.56) are the correct PRE-split figures (the 10-K/10-Q for those periods predate the split and were never retroactively restated), while Q1/Q2 2026 (794/770) are POST-split and correct. Verified directly against the Q2 2026 10-Q (bkng-20260630.htm) primary financial statements and the FY2025 10-K (bkng-20251231.htm); do not trust the CSV's SharesOutstanding column for BKNG without this context. NET DEBT: BKNG carries net DEBT (not net cash) at every recent balance-sheet date (~$3.0-4.0B), so per method 1(b) interest income is NOT stripped from FCF -- the net-cash-double-count trap does not apply here (net cash > 1x FCF base is the trigger, and this is the opposite sign). COMPONENT-BUILD RECONCILIATION (why last_fcf/margins differ from a naive reported_fcf-derived owner FCF): reported FY2025 FCF ($9,087M) run through the naive owner-FCF formula (reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes) gives ~$7,940M (29.5% margin), but roughly $1.7-2.2B of FY2025 operating cash flow is non-cash, non-operating add-back noise -- principally a $1,428M unrealized FX loss on Euro-denominated debt (which reversed to a $526M GAIN in FY2024: this line swings ~$2B year to year), a $457M one-off impairment, and $360M of convertible-note fair-value/discount amortization, partially offset by a $516M deferred-tax benefit. These are financing/FX items, not operating cash generation, and the method's component build (section 2) exists precisely to avoid carrying such one-offs forward. The component build anchored to FY2025's own actual adjusted-EBITDA-before-SBC margin (37.8%, per the 10-K segment note 'Segment Adjusted EBITDA less Capex' of $9,852M + capex $322M = $10,174M / $26,917M revenue) reconciles to an owner FCF of ~$6,833M (25.4% margin) at FY2025 actuals -- this is last_fcf, and it is the basis the forward projection is built from, NOT the naive $7,940M/29.5%-margin figure. Cash taxes paid have run 26-33% of pretax income the last three years (noisy, reflecting the same FX/convertible-note non-cash swings in the denominator), materially above the stable 19-22% GAAP effective tax rate the company has sustained on the Netherlands Innovation Box benefit and US federal credits; the model uses the GAAP effective rate (21%, base case) applied to EBIT as the more defensible, non-noisy cash-tax proxy for an unlevered flow. Working capital: FY2025 deferred-merchant-bookings increase ($796M) was substantially offset by accounts-receivable growth ($730M), netting to only ~$66M on a $2.2B revenue increase -- confirmed genuinely small (unlike a prepaid-subscription business), so wc_capture_pct = 0 in all three scenarios rather than assuming a deferred-revenue tailwind BKNG's merchant/agency mix does not actually deliver.

bear.narrative: AI-driven search (Google AI Overviews, emerging AI travel agents) structurally erodes the paid-search funnel Booking has monetized for two decades, forcing higher marketing spend just to defend traffic and compressing margin from 37.8% toward the mid-30s permanently. The EU DMA gatekeeper obligations and the 10,000+-hotel parity-clause litigation prove a genuine structural cost, not a one-off compliance exercise, and US state-level consumer-protection suits add further legal overhang. Global travel demand growth normalizes to low-single-digit as the post-COVID snapback fully laps out. The business remains solidly FCF-generative throughout (no zero-floor hit) -- this is a share-and-margin-erosion scenario, not a solvency scenario, consistent with BKNG's low net leverage even under stress.

base.narrative: High-single-digit revenue growth per management's own FY2026 algorithm (gross bookings, revenue and adjusted EBITDA all guided high-single-digit; adjusted EPS low-to-mid-teens on continued buybacks), decelerating gradually to 4% terminal as the OTA category matures. EBITDA margin (before SBC) continues the steady climb seen since FY2021 (26.6% -> 37.8%) as the Transformation Program's ~$650M run-rate savings land by end-FY2027, then flattens near 40% once that program is fully realized. Connected Trip cross-sell and AI-driven customer-service cost reduction are assumed to sustain modest margin expansion without requiring the alternative-accommodations or fintech bets to be transformative -- this is the 'guidance holds, nothing special happens' case.

bull.narrative: Connected Trip and AI investments deliver: cross-sell transactions (already growing >2x the base rate) pull basket size and retention meaningfully higher, voice-AI and engineering productivity gains compound the Transformation Program savings beyond the stated $650M target, and alternative-accommodations share gains plus fintech/payments penetration lift take rate. Booking successfully defends its traffic funnel against AI-search disintermediation (Genius loyalty and direct-traffic growth outpace any Google/AI-answer-engine erosion) and the EU DMA transition proves a compliance cost rather than a structural profit headwind. Requires several of these to go right simultaneously, which is why it is weighted below base.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default shaded slightly toward bear (20% vs the 15% default) given two live, high-severity structural risks flagged in the Analysis JSON that are specific to this company rather than generic macro caution: AI-search disintermediation of the OTA funnel (severity: high) and EU DMA gatekeeper obligations plus 10,000+-hotel parity-clause litigation (severity: high, fines up to 10-20% of global revenue for DMA breaches). Bull held at 30% (below the 35% default) because the bull case requires several independent things to go right at once (Connected Trip AND AI cost gains AND alternative-accommodations share gains AND a benign DMA outcome). Net leverage is low (~0.3x net debt/EBITDA) so bear weight is not pushed higher on solvency grounds -- the downside case here is margin/multiple compression, not going-concern risk.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
